# Why the ideas that did not join added nothing (generated by `cypmode/challenge/why_no_gain.py`)

Every row compares the default stack with the default stack plus one group of candidates, on the nested outer folds, with the weights and the corrected resampled t of the gates. The detectable effect is the smallest true AUC difference that a one-sided test at 5% detects with 80% power at the corrected standard error; the design floor is the same quantity with infinitely many repeats. Redundancy is the mean absolute Spearman correlation between the group's predictions and the default stack's on held-out rows. Weight is the share of the stack's absolute coefficients that falls on the group. The equivalence verdict compares the 90% interval of the change with +-0.01 AUC: *equivalent* means the idea adds nothing that matters, *inconclusive* means the design cannot tell.

Corrected p values of the 72 comparisons of ideas that did not join: 2 below 0.05 (about 3.6 would be expected if none carried an effect and the test were exact); counts in the five equal bins of [0, 1]: 16, 11, 11, 16, 18. The corrected test is conservative, so the counts rise towards 1.

Shapiro-Wilk p of the paired differences is below 0.05 in 68 of 148 comparisons; the t test assumes normally distributed differences.
